content.text: I have a branch that partially addresses this issue here:
https://github.com/acoburn/fcrepo-camel/tree/better-integration-tests
That is, the branch addresses only the first item listed above. (The third item, incidentally, is a bit complicated).
I will issue a pull request after this (
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-camel/pull/27)
is merged.
The branch has been updated to include integration tests with a Solr server (i.e. item #2)
I've added a pull request for this branch:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-camel/pull/28
This PR does not include integration tests in an OSGi environment. That will be addressed in another PR.
Build failure output in attached 'build.txt'.

I tried building the project on a mac with an empty ~/.m2 directory and also on a cleanly provisioned linux (centos) server (with openjdk-1.7.0 and the most recent maven3 from a.o). Both times the integration tests completed with no errors (meaning jetty started up cleanly), so I'm not able to reproduce what you're encountering.
That said, the error you describe appears to relate to slf4j bindings in the maven-jetty-plugin. Can you try adding these lines to pom.xml around line 428
<dependency>
<groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
<artifactId>slf4j-log4j12</artifactId>
<version>${slf4j.version}</version>
</dependency>
Does that fix things? All I can say is that this doesn't adversely affect my build (neither on centos nor on a mac).
Indeed, the following PR works for me:
https://github.com/acoburn/fcrepo-camel/pull/6
Oh, good. I've merged that PR into
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-camel/pull/28
Looks good, pending response to code-review comments.
@awoods I have updated the pull request based on your comments
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-camel/commit/a361ca163f4ee6a910f1fde9f72f879f0d4e123f
The integration tests for fcrepo-camel could be more thorough, and they could do a better job of independently checking the results of an external operation (such as saving data to a triplestore).
In particular, an embedded solr server should be set up as part of this
Also, an OSGi environment should test the deployability of the bundle.
